MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  March 10, 2020

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Goodell at 5:00 p.m., on March 10, 2020, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on March 5, 2020, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also posted
at Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and Norman P. Murray
Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Bucknum (arrived at 5:08 p.m.)
  Council Member Raths
  Council Member Sachs
  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley
  Mayor Goodell

Absent:  None

Staff Present: Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Legal Counsel: Existing Litigation Pursuant to Paragraph 4 of
  Subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9 - Southwest Voter Registration Education Project v.
  The City of Mission Viejo

  Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Discussed the timing of actions surrounding the Voters Rights Act
  lawsuit against the City of Mission Viejo. She outlined specific dates and expressed concerns
  with the intent of the City’s response.

CS2. Conference with Legal Counsel - Initiation of Litigation Pursuant to Paragraph (4) of
  Subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9: 1 case

City Council Minutes  1  March 10, 2020
 RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:06 p.m., Mayor Goodell recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:04 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the Council addressed two matters in Closed Session.
The Council received updates and gave direction to staff but no reportable actions occurred

INVOCATION: Council Member Raths

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Recognize the YMCA’s EPIC Mission Viejo Delegation for the Model Legislature &
  Court Program

  Mayor Goodell presented certificates of commendation to Lead Advisory Zach Brooks and
  members of the Epic Mission Viejo Delegation.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Cathy Palmer, M.V.: Voiced her concerns with Southern California Edison’s proposed rate
increase of 14.4% effective January 1, 2021. She encouraged the Council to support Community
Choice Energy (CCE) so residents will have a choice with their energy provider.

Maya Cappellino, L.R.: Asked that the City Council consider passing an ordinance that would
allow residential beekeeping within the City. She expressed concern over the decrease in the
honeybee population over the last 30 years.

The following spoke in support of allowing beekeeping within the City of Mission Viejo:
Dannielle Cappellino, Ladera Ranch.; Jennifer Byerly, Ladera Ranch; Liz Savage, Fullerton; Tom
Bogdan, Costa Mesa; Jonathan Scott, Lake Forest; Jim Noggle, Laguna Niguel; Pamela Fraser,
Laguna Niguel; David Raslowsky, Laguna Niguel; Michael Buyrley, M.V.; Robert Stone,
Newport Beach; and Mike Camaj, M.V.

Craig Owings, Karah Owings, Karisa Owings, and Lisa Owings, M.V.: spoke independently about
their R.V. and the pleasure they have had using it for family trips. They asked that the City Council
consider changing the rule to allow small R.V.’s to be parked on single loaded streets.

Ryan Farsai, Sheridan, OR: Spoke about the Corona Virus and gave his opinion of various ways
the community can avoid contracting it.

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

STAFF REPORTS

11. Mid-Year Budget Review for FY 2019-2020

  Administrative Services Manager Susan Knudson gave the staff report.

  Council Member Kelley asked that the motion include that $518,138 will go into the General

  the resolution be modified to include that Council directs that $518,138 is added to the
  General Fund Reserves.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars

City Council Minutes  4  March 10, 2020
 Council Member Bucknum

Council Member Bucknum asked staff to return to the City Council with an analysis and draft
ordinance that would modify the prohibition of beekeeping in neighborhoods. She asked that it
include any possible impacts to the City and recommended regulatory language for owner liability.
She also thanked everyone who attended the meeting this evening to speak on the topic. Council
Member Bucknum stated that she was remiss for not wearing her St. Patrick’s Day green since
there is not a Council Meeting until after the holiday. She reminded residents of the Irish fest on
March 14 at the Village Green and encouraged everyone to attend. Council Member Bucknum
noted that International Women’s Day was last week and she and Mayor Pro Tem Kelley attended
the Girls Softball opening night last Friday. She also attended Little League baseball opening day
where she threw the first pitch and she was pleased that the ball made it over home plate. In
conclusion, Council Member Bucknum announced that last weekend’s Oso Fit 5k Fun Run raised
$20,000 for local charities and was a wonderful event.

Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths commented on the bee farm his uncle had in Minnesota when he was
growing up and stated he is in favor of allowing bees for the honey they produce.

Council Member Sachs

Council Member Sachs addressed the Owings family desire to park their R.V. on their residential
street. He explained that the City Council passes ordinances that affect the totality of the
community and that is their job as elected officials. City Attorney Curley added that extensive
police services and code enforcement staff hours have been invested in this family’s issue. The
response was required due to a number of neighbors that felt their rights were being imposed-upon
and the City was therefore responsive to the neighborhood problem. He stated that there is a
violation of the City’s Municipal Code, along with the State Vehicle Code that applies to every
resident in California. Council Member Sachs commented on Mr. Owings statement that “for five
years we have been breaking the law and that sets a precedent.” He said it does not set a precedent
and that the police should be seen as those who enforce the law. Council Member Sachs noted that
it costs him money to store his R.V. He said that is a part of belonging to a community and obeying
the laws and ordinances of that community.

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley congratulated Council Member Greg Raths on his win in the 45th
Congressional District Primary Election and noted that he will move forward to the General
Election in November. She also congratulated Mission Viejo Nadadores Dive Team member
Avery Giese for being named one of the USA Diving 2020 High Performance Squad. Avery is 14
years-old and one of under 30 kids in the United States, the only one from the Mission Viejo
Nadadores and the only one of two selected divers from California. Avery won the Nationals last
summer and Mayor Pro Tem Kelley asked the Mayor to recognize Avery at a future Council
Meeting. She also announced that the Marine Adoption Committee is hosting “Wine Tasting and
Music” which will benefit the City’s Adopted Marine Battalion. The event is Sunday, March 15,
2020, from 3:00 to 5:00 p.m. at Norman P. Murray Community Center. Tickets are $30 and can
be purchased online at mvcommunityfoundation.org or at the front desk at Community Center.

City Council Minutes  5  March 10, 2020
 Council Member Kelley outlined her attendance at the 2020 Tri-Chamber Mixer, hosted by three
of the local Chambers of Commerce. It was a nice event and good to see the City’s businesses
represented. She was also Principal for a Day at Newhart Middle School where she was a former
PTA President and her three children attended middle school. She said she loved going back to see
the improvements that have been made at the school and also the strong academic program. Mayor
Pro Tem Kelley announced that there will be a ground breaking celebration for the new STEM
Building at Newhart in the near future. She also discussed her recent visit to Oxford Preparatory
Academy where she provided certificates of commendation to the students who came out on a
rainy day to plant more than 600 plants at Pavion Park. She said she attended the opening day
ceremony for Mission Viejo Girls Softball and had a fun time and lastly, she discussed her
attendance at the Women of Influence Awards last week where Amy Potter, CFO of the Toll Road
Agencies, was nominated.

Mayor Goodell

Mayor Goodell complimented Maya Cappellino on her beekeeping presentation this evening. He
thanked Council Member Bucknum for asking staff to follow up with a report and draft ordinance
for beekeeping within the City. He announced that he was Principal for a Day at Capistrano Valley
High School and he attended a Town Hall Meeting for elected officials at the County of Orange
regarding the COVID-19 virus where they heard information from the Centers for Disease Control
(CDC) and the Orange County Health Care Agency (OCHCA). Mayor Goodell informed residents
that the latest updates and information on the virus can be found at ochealthinfo.com. He also
discussed precautions for avoiding the virus and asked residents not to panic. Mayor Goodell
announced that the Swimming Junior Olympics event was cancelled at the Rose Bowl Aquatics
Center in Pasadena due to the COVID-19 outbreak. The City of Mission Viejo has been asked if
the event could be held at the Marguerite Aquatics Center and staff is waiting on word from the
CDC before granting the request. Council Member Bucknum interjected that the Senior Day event
that was scheduled for Friday, March 13, at Norman P. Murray Community Center has been
postponed.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 7:54 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Goodell adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, March 24, 2020, at 5:00 p.m.

Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk
